sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.zh: 罗曼，你平时服用什么处方药吗？

sentences.en: Do you take Gernavex?
sentences.zh: 你吃Gernavex吗？

sentences.en: This is Sean Cole, everybody.
sentences.zh: 各位，这位是肖恩·科尔。

sentences.zh: 他是我的老朋友，也是节目的老朋友。

sentences.zh: 你吃Extensor吗？

sentences.en: Or Zyaflex?
sentences.zh: 或者Zyaflex？

sentences.en: What is going on?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Ask your doctor.
sentences.zh: 去问你的医生。

sentences.zh: 去问你的医生关于Xdenvy的事。

sentences.en: Ask your doctor about Nexplanon.
sentences.zh: 去问你的医生关于Nexplanon的事。

sentences.en: Ask about Repatha.
sentences.zh: 问问Repatha。

sentences.en: Ask about Nucala.
sentences.zh: 问问Nucala。

sentences.en: Ask your doctor about Kaplida.
sentences.zh: 去问你的医生关于Kaplida的事。

sentences.en: Help see more of the light inside of...
sentences.zh: 帮助看到更多内在的光芒……

sentences.en: Okay, Sean, why are we talking about this?
sentences.zh: 好了，肖恩，我们为什么要谈论这个？

sentences.en: So the reason I'm sitting here with you today can pretty much be boiled down to the Seinfeldian question,
sentences.zh: 我今天坐在这里和你谈话的原因，基本上可以归结为那个“宋飞式”的问题：

sentences.en: what is the deal with pharmaceutical brand names?
sentences.zh: 医药品牌名到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: It's like watching TV in the middle of the day can make you feel like you've had a partial stroke
sentences.zh: 就像在白天看电视，会让你感觉自己好像轻微中风了一样，

sentences.en: that scrambled half the words on the screen,
sentences.zh: 屏幕上的一半文字都变得乱七八糟，

sentences.en: which is ironic considering that that's probably what some of the drugs they're advertising are supposed to prevent.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他们广告里推销的某些药物本应是用来预防中风的，这还挺讽刺的。

sentences.en: Once Monthly EbbGliss is a treatment that can be used with or without topicals.
sentences.zh: “每月一次的EbbGliss”是一种可以配合或不配合外用药使用的疗法。

sentences.en: Dupixin can help you stay ahead of Xdenvy.
sentences.zh: Dupixin可以帮助你领先于Xdenvy。

sentences.zh: Ingressive。

sentences.zh: Kobanfi。

sentences.zh: Pristique。

sentences.zh: Capvexiv。

sentences.zh: Cabanova。

sentences.en: Jardians.
sentences.zh: Jardians。

sentences.en: Maybe we don't need a pill for everything.
sentences.zh: 也许我们并不需要什么药都吃。

sentences.en: You can say that again, Kenan Thompson.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，基南·汤普森。

sentences.en: But for managing weight, there's Wagovi.
sentences.zh: 但对于体重管理，有Wagovi。

sentences.en: The first and only...
sentences.zh: 第一个也是唯一一个……

sentences.en: It's funny that Kenan did a real pharmaceutical ad,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，基南确实拍过真正的医药广告，

sentences.en: given that he was also in this Saturday Night Live sketch about a fake hormone supplement for women.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他还在《周六夜现场》里演过一个关于女性虚假激素补充剂的小品。

sentences.en: There's a new drug for gals over four.
sentences.zh: 有一种针对四岁以上女性的新药。

sentences.en: It's called the Jade.
sentences.zh: 它叫Jade。

sentences.en: It's the Jordan.
sentences.zh: 它叫Jordan。

sentences.en: Whatever, just dance.
sentences.zh: 管它呢，跳舞就行了。

sentences.en: So we all laugh about these drugs, but the question becomes,
sentences.zh: 所以我们都在嘲笑这些药，但问题在于，

sentences.en: why do they all sound like Star Trek villains?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们听起来都像《星际迷航》里的反派？

sentences.en: Is that by design?
sentences.zh: 这是刻意设计的吗？

sentences.en: Is it necessary for some reason?
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因这是必要的吗？

sentences.en: Is it simply wrong-headed on the part of the marketers?
sentences.zh: 还是说这纯粹是营销人员的错误想法？

sentences.en: I mean, those are a lot of questions, but do you have some answers for those questions?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这些问题很多，但你对这些问题有什么答案吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I got to the bottom of it.
sentences.zh: 有的，我查清了真相。

sentences.en: And I'll just say, underneath the noisiness of the names,
sentences.zh: 我只想说，在这些名字嘈杂的外表下，

sentences.en: is not just a logic that you'd never guess is in operation.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅有一种你永远猜不到的逻辑在运作。

sentences.en: In a lot of cases, there's, I know how this is going to sound,
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，我知道这听起来会怎样，

sentences.en: an actual poetry going on that I never imagined,
sentences.zh: 其实有一种我从未想象过的诗意在其中，

sentences.en: and that I now want everybody else to be thinking about the next time they see one of those ads.
sentences.zh: 我现在想让大家下次看到这些广告时，都能思考一下这一点。

sentences.en: That's a big claim when you're talking about brand names of drugs.
sentences.zh: 当你谈论药物品牌名时，这可是个宏大的说法。

sentences.en: I'm, okay, but just hear me out.
sentences.zh: 我，好吧，但请听我说完。

sentences.en: We'll see what you think at the end.
sentences.zh: 最后你会怎么想，我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: But just to start at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 但还是从头说起吧。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Scott?
sentences.zh: 斯科特？

sentences.en: Yes, Sean.
sentences.zh: 是我，肖恩。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: This is Scott Piergrosi, who is in practically every article you read about pharmaceutical brand names.
sentences.zh: 这位是斯科特·皮尔格罗西，你读到的关于医药品牌名的文章里几乎都有他。

sentences.en: And there's a reason for that.
sentences.zh: 这是有原因的。

sentences.en: He's the head of creative at the Brand Institute, which is kind of a clearinghouse.
sentences.zh: 他是Brand Institute的创意总监，那地方算是个集散中心。

sentences.en: They helped name more than 75% of the new drugs on the market in a given year.
sentences.zh: 他们每年帮助命名市场上超过75%的新药。

sentences.en: One company.
sentences.zh: 一家公司。

sentences.en: Yep, at least according to them.
sentences.zh: 没错，至少他们是这么说的。

sentences.en: 75% of both brand names and generic names, too, which are even longer and wilder sounding, as you know.
sentences.zh: 75%的品牌名和通用名，如你所知，通用名听起来更长、更狂野。

sentences.en: They have a separate department for generics or non-proprietary.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个专门负责通用名或非专利名的部门。

sentences.en: They get upset when you say generics.
sentences.zh: 你说“通用名”他们会不高兴的。

sentences.en: Non-proprietary names.
sentences.zh: 非专利名。

sentences.en: But we are focusing on the brand names, the Brand Institute names.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在关注的是品牌名，也就是Brand Institute命名的那些。

sentences.en: Can I also respectfully correct you and say it's just Brand Institute?
sentences.zh: 我能冒昧地纠正你一下吗，应该叫Brand Institute，不用加那个定冠词？

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lose the the.
sentences.zh: 去掉那个“the”。

sentences.en: It's cleaner.
sentences.zh: 这样更简洁。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Scott's been at Brand Institute for more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 斯科特在Brand Institute工作了20多年了。

sentences.en: And I just asked him to, you know, take me through the process from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我请他带我从头了解一下整个流程。

sentences.en: Like, where do they even start naming a drug?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们到底是怎么开始给药命名的？

sentences.en: Have you ever seen the movie Brain Candy?
sentences.zh: 你看过电影《Brain Candy》吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Should I?
sentences.zh: 我应该看吗？

sentences.en: You should see it, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 你绝对应该看看。

sentences.en: This is a Kids in the Hall movie.
sentences.zh: 这是“Kids in the Hall”的一部电影。

sentences.en: That's Kids in the Hall, the sketch comedy troupe from Canada.
sentences.zh: 那是“Kids in the Hall”，来自加拿大的素描喜剧团。

sentences.en: And Brain Candy was about a new antidepressant drug that came to market.
sentences.zh: 《Brain Candy》讲的是一种新上市的抗抑郁药。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, but they have a scene where the marketing guy comes into the boardroom and he tells the story of how he thought of the name.
sentences.zh: 他们有个场景，营销人员走进董事会，讲述他是如何想出这个名字的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I was driving around last night in my $62,000 car and I'm trying to think up a name for the drug.
sentences.zh: 昨晚我开着我那辆6.2万美元的车到处转，想给药起个名字。

sentences.en: And suddenly it hit me.
sentences.zh: 突然我灵光一现。

sentences.en: The name?
sentences.zh: 名字？

sentences.en: No, a bird.
sentences.zh: 不，是一只鸟。

sentences.en: It hit my windshield.
sentences.zh: 它撞上了我的挡风玻璃。

sentences.en: When that happened, I got depressed.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，我抑郁了。

sentences.en: Not you, Cisco.
sentences.zh: 不是你，西斯科。

sentences.en: Yeah, even me.
sentences.zh: 是的，连我也抑郁了。

sentences.en: But as soon as I got depressed, I got undepressed.
sentences.zh: 但当我抑郁的时候，我立刻又“不抑郁”了。

sentences.en: Because as I was cleaning the gleaming guts of that bird off my windshield, I thought of the name for the drug.
sentences.zh: 因为当我清理挡风玻璃上那只鸟的内脏时，我想到了药的名字。

sentences.en: And he says, gleamanex.
sentences.zh: 他说，Gleamanex。

sentences.en: And everyone does like a slow applause.
sentences.zh: 然后大家都开始缓慢地鼓掌。

sentences.en: And it's the opposite of how it actually works.
sentences.zh: 这和实际的工作方式完全相反。

sentences.en: How it actually works is much more rigorous and time consuming.
sentences.zh: 实际的工作方式要严谨得多，也耗时得多。

sentences.en: They meet with the client, be it Pfizer or Amgen or whomever, kind of get a sense as to what they're thinking.
sentences.zh: 他们会和客户开会，无论是辉瑞、安进还是其他公司，了解他们的想法。

sentences.en: And from there, Brand Institute assigns a small team to come up with an initial list of like 300 to 500 ideas on their own.
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，Brand Institute会指派一个小团队，自己先想出300到500个初始创意。

sentences.en: 500 names.
sentences.zh: 500个名字。

sentences.en: That's a lot of brainstorming for names that will not get used.
sentences.zh: 对于那些最终不会被使用的名字来说，这真是大量的头脑风暴。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And at that point, the job is pretty much just figuring out which ones are actually viable and good enough to test out with the client.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上，工作基本上就是找出哪些名字真正可行，好到可以拿去给客户测试。

sentences.en: It's funny because clients will say, just give me an easy to pronounce name and we'll call this a win.
sentences.zh: 很有趣，因为客户会说，只要给我一个容易发音的名字，我们就当赢了。

sentences.en: And then we present a slide, let's say, of 25.
sentences.zh: 然后我们展示一张幻灯片，比如有25个名字。

sentences.en: And we'll be lucky if we get to retain two of them.
sentences.zh: 能留下两个就算走运了。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: They are all solely easy to pronounce.
sentences.zh: 它们明明都很好发音。

sentences.en: And the client just like, meh, I just don't like it.
sentences.zh: 客户就会说，呃，我就是不喜欢。

sentences.en: And I'm like, but that's what you asked for.
sentences.zh: 我说，但这正是你们要求的啊。

sentences.en: Just remember that.
sentences.zh: 记住这一点。

sentences.en: That's what you asked for.
sentences.zh: 这正是你们要求的。

sentences.en: Because why don't they like those ones?
sentences.zh: 那为什么他们不喜欢那些名字呢？

sentences.en: Like what is it when they say no?
sentences.zh: 当他们说“不”的时候，到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: They can't see it.
sentences.zh: 他们看不出来。

sentences.en: They can't see it as the product.
sentences.zh: 他们看不出这名字能代表产品。

sentences.en: It doesn't fit.
sentences.zh: 不合适。

sentences.en: And how are they generating these ideas in the first place?
sentences.zh: 那他们最初是怎么产生这些创意的呢？

sentences.en: Like when they're coming up with all these ideas, where are the ideas coming from?
sentences.zh: 当他们想出这些点子时，灵感是从哪来的？

sentences.en: Well, historically how it worked was everybody was just sort of forging omnivorously anywhere and everywhere for different combinations of words and letters.
sentences.zh: 历史上，大家都是在到处搜罗，贪婪地寻找各种单词和字母的组合。

sentences.en: Magazines, foreign language dictionaries, another company I read about.
sentences.zh: 杂志、外语词典，我读到过另一家公司也是这样。

sentences.en: So not Brand Institute, but a competitor.
sentences.zh: 不是Brand Institute，而是竞争对手。

sentences.en: So they sometimes leaf through cowboy dictionaries and surfer dictionaries.
sentences.zh: 他们有时会翻阅牛仔词典和冲浪者词典。

sentences.en: What's a cowboy dictionary?
sentences.zh: 什么是牛仔词典？

sentences.en: I looked it up.
sentences.zh: 我查过了。

sentences.en: There's one from 1968 called Western Words by Ramon F.
sentences.zh: 有一本1968年的书叫《西部词汇》，作者是拉蒙·F·亚当斯。

sentences.en: AdaMs.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: A little horse is soon curried.
sentences.zh: “小马很快就会被刷洗干净。”

sentences.en: I'll take your word for it.
sentences.zh: 我姑且信你。

sentences.en: Brand Institute has also started using an AI platform called Brandy.
sentences.zh: Brand Institute也开始使用一个叫Brandy的AI平台。

sentences.en: Cute.
sentences.zh: 挺可爱的。

sentences.en: That's just helping out with the initial phase of the process.
sentences.zh: 那只是在流程的初始阶段提供帮助。

sentences.en: Scott says a lot of the work is still done by humans.
sentences.zh: 斯科特说，大部分工作仍然是由人类完成的。

sentences.en: You might explore types of names like palindromes or anagraMs.
sentences.zh: 你可以探索一些命名方式，比如回文或变位词。

sentences.en: One of the more helpful exercises we do is we try to get the client to state, like if it's on the cover of Time magazine, for example, what would the headline say?
sentences.zh: 我们最有效的练习之一，就是让客户设想，如果这药上了《时代》杂志封面，标题会怎么写？

sentences.en: And then we actually might even try to mold that expression into a name.
sentences.zh: 然后我们甚至会尝试把那个表达方式塑造成一个名字。

sentences.en: Hang on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: So you would try to take that sentence?
sentences.zh: 所以你会尝试用那个句子？

sentences.en: Yeah, so let's say a drug alters your course in life, AltaCourse.
sentences.zh: 对，比方说，如果一种药能改变你的人生轨迹，就叫 AltaCourse。

sentences.en: So that name is still-
sentences.zh: 所以那个名字还是——

sentences.en: I want a drug that does that, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我想要一种那样的药。

sentences.en: If I could take AltaCourse, boy, oh boy.
sentences.zh: 如果我能吃 AltaCourse，天哪，天哪。

sentences.en: AltaCourse.
sentences.zh: AltaCourse。

sentences.en: Or they could look at the drug and say, okay, what is the hopeful outcome of taking this thing?
sentences.zh: 或者他们可以审视这种药，问自己：服用此药的理想结果是什么？

sentences.en: And then explore that from a bunch of different angles.
sentences.zh: 然后从多个不同的角度去探索。

sentences.en: So, for example, sleep aids.
sentences.zh: 比如，安眠药。

sentences.en: They could say, okay, this is a drug that helps you stay asleep through the night.
sentences.zh: 他们可以说，好吧，这是一种能帮你整晚安睡的药。

sentences.en: Or this is a drug that leaves you feeling refreshed in the morning.
sentences.zh: 或者，这是一种能让你在早晨感到神清气爽的药。

sentences.en: Same section of the drugstore, two different ways of looking at it.
sentences.zh: 在药店的同一个货架区，却有两种不同的切入点。

sentences.en: So, for example, there's Lunesta, a drug that Scott's company named.
sentences.zh: 比如 Lunesta，就是斯科特公司命名的一种药。

sentences.en: The reason Lunesta works is because of the lunar imagery.
sentences.zh: Lunesta 之所以有效，是因为它运用了月亮的意象。

sentences.en: The suffix, esta, has an inference of restorative sleep.
sentences.zh: 后缀 -esta 暗示了恢复性的睡眠。

sentences.en: As in C-esta.
sentences.zh: 就像 C-esta 一样。

sentences.en: Ah, okay, very cool.
sentences.zh: 啊，明白了，太酷了。

sentences.en: See what they're doing there?
sentences.zh: 看出他们是怎么做的了吗？

sentences.en: But really the lunar is what anchored it, so nighttime sleep.
sentences.zh: 但真正起到锚定作用的是“月亮”，即夜间睡眠。

sentences.en: Within the category, you have Ambien.
sentences.zh: 在同一类别里，还有 Ambien。

sentences.en: What is Ambien?
sentences.zh: Ambien 是什么？

sentences.en: It's A-M-B-N.
sentences.zh: 它是 A-M-B-N。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好（Good morning）。

sentences.en: So that's the good morning.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是“早上好”。

sentences.en: Then you have newer products like Balsamra.
sentences.zh: 还有像 Belsomra 这样的新产品。

sentences.en: That's a beautiful night's sleep with Balsamra.
sentences.zh: Belsomra 代表美好的夜晚睡眠。

sentences.en: Bel-som is somnus, which is sleep in Latin.
sentences.zh: Bel-som 源自 somnus，在拉丁语中是睡眠的意思。

sentences.en: Then there's other sources of little name-building blocks.
sentences.zh: 还有其他构建名字的素材来源。

sentences.en: They might grab a few letters from the generic name of the drug or the active ingredient.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会从药物的通用名或活性成分中提取几个字母。

sentences.en: And, for example, bupropion hydrochloride.
sentences.zh: 比如，盐酸安非他酮（bupropion hydrochloride）。

sentences.en: That's the active ingredient in the antidepressant Welbutrin.
sentences.zh: 这是抗抑郁药 Welbutrin 的活性成分。

sentences.en: And then sometimes the name is derived from the science of how the drug works.
sentences.zh: 有时名字源于药物的作用科学。

sentences.en: A lot of cancer drugs are like that, Scott says, because the audience is really more the doctor than the patient in those cases.
sentences.zh: 斯科特说，很多抗癌药都是这样，因为在这些案例中，受众其实主要是医生而非患者。

sentences.en: So oftentimes we want to highlight what's unique about that product from a scientific standpoint because that will resonate with oncologists.
sentences.zh: 所以我们通常想从科学角度突出产品的独特性，因为这会引起肿瘤科医生的共鸣。

sentences.en: And about half of new cancer therapies are derived from the mechanism of action, so the science behind the drug.
sentences.zh: 大约一半的新型癌症疗法都是根据作用机制，也就是药物背后的科学原理来命名的。

sentences.en: That is what the drug is actually doing and to what part of you.
sentences.zh: 这就是药物实际的作用方式以及它作用于你身体的哪个部位。

sentences.en: So there's this one drug called Imdeltra.
sentences.zh: 有一种药叫 Imdeltra。

sentences.en: It's I-M-D-E-L-L-T-R-A.
sentences.zh: 它是 I-M-D-E-L-L-T-R-A。

sentences.en: Imdeltra is a DLL-3 immunotherapy.
sentences.zh: Imdeltra 是一种 DLL-3 免疫疗法。

sentences.en: Well, of course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然了。

sentences.en: I mean, everybody knows about that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，大家都知道那个。

sentences.en: So the double L's and the TRU suggesting three is so intentional to represent the mechanism of action of the product quite elegantly.
sentences.zh: 所以双 L 和暗示数字 3 的 TRU 是非常刻意的，非常优雅地表现了产品的科学作用机制。

sentences.en: And if Scott Pierre-Grossi sounds ever so slightly defensive about the name Imdeltra, it's because another drug namer I talked to did not agree with him.
sentences.zh: 如果斯科特·皮埃尔-格罗西（Scott Pierre-Grossi）听起来对 Imdeltra 这个名字有点防御性，那是因为我采访的另一位药物命名专家并不认同他。

sentences.en: It satisfies a meaning, but look how it looks, and that doesn't really look that good.
sentences.zh: 它满足了某种含义，但你看它的样子，看起来真的不怎么样。

sentences.en: Imdeltra.
sentences.zh: Imdeltra。

sentences.en: It's hard even to say.
sentences.zh: 甚至很难读出来。

sentences.en: Okay, so who's this?
sentences.zh: 好的，那这位是谁？

sentences.en: I am Arlene Tech.
sentences.zh: 我是阿琳·泰克（Arlene Tech）。

sentences.en: I have worked in brand naming for 30 plus years, most of those naming pharmaceuticals.
sentences.zh: 我在品牌命名领域工作了 30 多年，其中大部分时间都在为医药产品命名。

sentences.en: Arlene is kind of a legend in pharmaceutical branding, and once I learned a little bit about her and her background,
sentences.zh: 阿琳在医药品牌界算是一位传奇人物，当我了解了一些关于她和她的背景后，

sentences.en: I couldn't not reach out to her to get her perspective on how prescription drugs get their names.
sentences.zh: 我忍不住要联系她，听听她对处方药如何命名的看法。

sentences.en: And does she sort of predate the Brand Institute style of naming?
sentences.zh: 她算是早于 Brand Institute 那种命名风格的人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, she's like an OG.
sentences.zh: 是的，她是鼻祖级人物。

sentences.en: And unlike Brand Institute, with its teams of 15 people or whatever, the places Arlene's worked, people tend to tackle projects on their own.
sentences.zh: 而且与拥有 15 人团队的 Brand Institute 不同，阿琳工作过的地方，人们往往倾向于独立完成项目。

sentences.en: And just to give you another picture of how drug names are invented, there's this one drug she was assigned back in 1992 that was for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
sentences.zh: 为了让你更直观地了解药物名称是如何发明的，她 1992 年曾负责过一种治疗良性前列腺增生的药物。

sentences.en: Enlarged prostate, basically, which makes it difficult to pee.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是前列腺肥大，导致排尿困难。

sentences.en: In trying to figure out what to name this drug, Arlene ran a focus group with a bunch of urologists.
sentences.zh: 在构思这个药名时，阿琳组织了一场由多位泌尿科医生参加的焦点小组讨论。

sentences.en: And this one doctor in particular said something that stuck with her.
sentences.zh: 其中一位医生说的话让她印象深刻。

sentences.en: It was at the end of the group, and I asked the doctor, what's it like when the drug worked and the guy got well?
sentences.zh: 那是小组讨论快结束时，我问医生：当药物起效、病人康复时，那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And the doctor said, visualize a strong stream.
sentences.zh: 医生说，想象一股强劲的尿流。

sentences.en: A strong stream of urine.
sentences.zh: 一股强劲的尿流。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So when I was home and I was writing the notes up, I thought to myself, well, a strong stream, that would be vigorous.
sentences.zh: 所以当我回家整理笔记时，我心想，强劲的尿流，那应该是“有力的”（vigorous）。

sentences.en: And the first thing I could think of that was a stream like that was Niagara.
sentences.zh: 我能想到的第一个像那样流动的词就是尼亚加拉大瀑布（Niagara）。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I put vigorous plus Niagara equals Viagra.
sentences.zh: 所以我把 vigorous 加上 Niagara，就成了 Viagra。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I met the woman who named Viagra.
sentences.zh: 我见到了给伟哥命名的人。

sentences.en: She gave me her pen.
sentences.zh: 她把她的笔送给了我。

sentences.en: I'm going to keep it forever and ever.
sentences.zh: 我要永远永远珍藏它。

sentences.en: But wait a second.
sentences.zh: 但等一下。

sentences.en: So Viagra is for erectile dysfunction, not like the enlarged prostate that makes it hard for you to pee.
sentences.zh: 伟哥是治勃起功能障碍的，不是治那种让你排尿困难的前列腺肥大的。

sentences.en: So what is that about?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this is where this naming business gets even more complicated.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个命名行业变得更加复杂的地方。

sentences.en: Super interesting trick of the industry, just to digress here for a second.
sentences.zh: 这是业内一个超级有趣的把戏，先跑个题。

sentences.en: So Arlene came up with the name Viagra for this drug to treat prostate enlargement.
sentences.zh: 阿琳为这种治疗前列腺肥大的药想出了 Viagra 这个名字。

sentences.en: But for a lot of complicated reasons, they didn't end up using the name Viagra for that benign prostatic hyperplasia drug.
sentences.zh: 但由于许多复杂的原因，他们最终没有把 Viagra 这个名字用在那种治疗良性前列腺增生的药上。

sentences.en: And as far as Arlene knows, they just held on to the name.
sentences.zh: 据阿琳所知，他们只是把这个名字留着了。

sentences.en: It's true that companies can bank names in certain circumstances and use them later when a better fit comes along.
sentences.zh: 确实，公司在某些情况下会储备名字，等以后有更合适的产品时再用。

sentences.en: And around that same time, Pfizer was testing a completely different drug, which had nothing to do with the prostate.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时间，辉瑞公司正在测试一种完全不同的药物，与前列腺毫无关系。

sentences.en: That drug was supposed to treat angina, which is chest pain due to a heart condition.
sentences.zh: 那种药本意是治疗心绞痛，即心脏病引起的胸痛。

sentences.en: And the test was very successful.
sentences.zh: 测试非常成功。

sentences.en: Everybody was complying with it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都很配合。

sentences.en: And some of the guys came back and asked for more.
sentences.zh: 有些男士回来要求再多给点药。

sentences.en: Because, well, it didn't work very well for angina.
sentences.zh: 因为，嗯，它对心绞痛效果并不好。

sentences.en: It did have this crazy side effect.
sentences.zh: 但它确实有一个疯狂的副作用。

sentences.en: I think the medical term for it is lumpy trousers.
sentences.zh: 我想医学术语叫“裤裆隆起”。

sentences.en: And so they thought, well, that would be a much better way to sell this drug if it did that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想，如果这药有这种效果，那卖起来肯定好得多。

sentences.en: And they tried to do the whole thing right.
sentences.zh: 他们试图把一切都做对。

sentences.en: They tried to have a focus group.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试组织一个焦点小组。

sentences.en: A focus group to name their new miracle erection drug.
sentences.zh: 一个为他们的新奇迹勃起药命名的焦点小组。

sentences.en: And the names that came up just weren't that good.
sentences.zh: 但想出来的名字都不怎么样。

sentences.en: They were either too overtly sexual.
sentences.zh: 要么太露骨了。

sentences.en: And then some of the names were just not male enough.
sentences.zh: 要么就是不够有“男人味”。

sentences.en: If you want to sell a drug to Treat E.D., it should have a pretty masculine name.
sentences.zh: 如果你想卖一种治疗 ED（勃起功能障碍）的药，它应该有一个相当阳刚的名字。

sentences.en: And they just so happened to have the one that Arlene thought up stored away.
sentences.zh: 而他们恰好存着阿琳想出来的那个名字。

sentences.en: So they went with that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就用了那个。

sentences.en: So how does it feel to have named Viagra?
sentences.zh: 那么，给伟哥命名是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Different.
sentences.zh: 不一样。

sentences.en: Different than having not named Viagra?
sentences.zh: 和没给伟哥命名有什么不同？

sentences.en: Well, as my husband always used to say, I'm married to the Viagra woman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我丈夫常说的，我嫁给了“伟哥女士”。

sentences.en: That could mean a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 那含义可丰富了。

sentences.en: Yes, it could.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: Well, I have also told people that I have a one-word resume.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也告诉过别人，我的简历只有一个词。

sentences.en: You know, what's funny about that story is that it really is a lot more like that scene in the Kids in the Hall movie where the guy comes up with gleam an ex.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那个故事有趣的地方在于，它真的很像电影《少年当自强》（Kids in the Hall）里的那个场景，那个人想出了 Gleam-an-ex 这个名字。

sentences.en: I mean, she was just like trying to think of a name for a drug.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她当时只是在努力想一个药名。

sentences.en: And then this thing happened and it made her think of another thing and it led her to the name Viagra.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了这件事，让她想到了另一件事，最终引出了 Viagra 这个名字。

sentences.en: It really is much more like that.
sentences.zh: 真的非常像那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So why can't all drugs, you know, have that same approachability?
sentences.zh: 那为什么不是所有的药都能有那种亲和力呢？

sentences.en: Like Viagra is a very approachable name.
sentences.zh: 比如 Viagra 就是一个非常有亲和力的名字。

sentences.en: Lunesta is an approachable name.
sentences.zh: Lunesta 也是一个有亲和力的名字。

sentences.en: But why aren't they still?
sentences.zh: 但为什么现在不是这样了？

sentences.en: Like when you started, you started naming all these things like Skrillex or something, you know?
sentences.zh: 就像你刚开始的时候，你开始命名所有这些像 Skrillex 之类的东西，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Skrillex is a DJ.
sentences.zh: Skrillex 是个 DJ。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I think you mean Sky Rizzy.
sentences.zh: 我想你是说 Skyrizi。

sentences.en: Okay, Sky Rizzy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，Skyrizi。

sentences.en: And, you know, Wagovi, whatever.
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道，Wegovy 之类的。

sentences.en: Like, how do we get to there?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么变成这样的？

sentences.en: Okay, so just to start back in time a bit, even farther back from when Arlene named Viagra.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们回到过去，比阿琳给伟哥命名的时候还要早一点。

sentences.en: So, the big bang of pharmaceutical naming, as Scott Piergrosi calls it, comes in 1988 with the introduction of Prozac.
sentences.zh: 正如斯科特·皮埃尔-格罗西所说，医药命名的“大爆炸”发生在 1988 年，随着百忧解（Prozac）的推出。

sentences.en: That was the first real blockbuster name.
sentences.zh: 那是第一个真正意义上的大片级名字。

sentences.en: It's short, punchy, and it was all about marketing as opposed to even indicating what the drug did.
sentences.zh: 它简短、有力，而且完全是为了营销，而不是为了说明药物的用途。

sentences.en: It was what they now call a blank canvas or empty vessel type name.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们现在所说的“空白画布”或“空容器”类型的名字。

sentences.en: Obviously, it caught the public attention, became a household word.
sentences.zh: 显然，它吸引了公众的注意，成为了家喻户晓的词汇。

sentences.en: The guy who named it, David Wood, is now in the Medical Advertising Hall of Fame.
sentences.zh: 给它命名的人大卫·伍德（David Wood）现在已入选医学广告名人堂。

sentences.en: There's actually a Medical Advertising Hall of Fame.
sentences.zh: 实际上确实有一个医学广告名人堂。

sentences.en: Of course, there's a Medical Advertising Hall of Fame.
sentences.zh: 当然，确实有医学广告名人堂。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: David Wood died in 2007.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德于 2007 年去世。

sentences.en: And Arlene was really a protege of his.
sentences.zh: 阿琳确实是他的门生。

sentences.en: She worked really closely with him.
sentences.zh: 她和他合作得非常紧密。

sentences.en: Basically, I think he was trying to do a name that was semi-abstract.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我认为他当时想做一个半抽象的名字。

sentences.en: Everybody knew that the word pro meant something positive, you were for something.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道 pro 这个词意味着积极，表示你支持某事。

sentences.en: And the zac was simply a syllable that woke people up.
sentences.zh: 而 zac 仅仅是一个能让人清醒的音节。

sentences.en: It's like zap, zang, zip.
sentences.zh: 就像 zap、zang、zip 一样。

sentences.en: Well, the K sound on the end, zac, had a sharpness to it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，结尾的 K 音，zac，有一种尖锐感。

sentences.en: You know, a sharp sound might indicate something that was more targeted.
sentences.zh: 你知道，尖锐的声音可能暗示着更有针对性。

sentences.en: So, that year, 1988, only 17 drugs were approved by the FDA for therapeutic use.
sentences.zh: 所以，那一年，1988 年，FDA 仅批准了 17 种药物用于治疗。

sentences.en: 17 prescription drugs that needed brand names.
sentences.zh: 17 种需要品牌名称的处方药。

sentences.en: And that number has just trended upward over the years.
sentences.zh: 而这个数字多年来一直在上升。

sentences.en: So, last year, almost 50 new drugs hit the market.
sentences.zh: 所以，去年有近 50 种新药上市。

sentences.en: Number of letters in the alphabet, still 26.
sentences.zh: 字母表里的字母数量，还是26个。

sentences.en: And, like, why are there so many more drugs being approved now?
sentences.zh: 而且，为什么现在获批的药物越来越多了？

sentences.en: Just sheer growth in the industry, for one thing.
sentences.zh: 首先，这纯粹是因为行业规模的扩张。

sentences.en: More and more drugs being developed.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的药物被研发出来。

sentences.en: Especially with cancer.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在癌症领域。

sentences.en: There's a big push on that front.
sentences.zh: 这方面有很大的推动力。

sentences.en: And then a few other reasons that, believe me, are too wonky even for this show.
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些原因，相信我，对这个节目来说太深奥了。

sentences.en: I'm going to try not to take that personally.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不往心里去。

sentences.en: Please don't.
sentences.zh: 请别往心里去。

sentences.en: But, meanwhile, the Scots and the Orleans of the world are trying to accomplish something that, in this climate, just gets harder and harder.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，像斯科特（Scots）和阿琳（Orleans）这样的人，正试图在当前的环境下完成一件越来越难的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, in every case, they want to come up with something totally new, if they can manage it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在任何情况下，如果能做到的话，他们都想出一个全新的名字。

sentences.en: A singularly unique name is the goal.
sentences.zh: 目标是一个独一无二的名字。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Trademarkability, for one thing.
sentences.zh: 首先是为了商标注册的可行性。

sentences.en: And just plain marketability.
sentences.zh: 还有就是纯粹的市场推广需求。

sentences.en: They want the product to stand out.
sentences.zh: 他们希望产品能够脱颖而出。

sentences.en: But the main factor driving this ceaseless crusade for nominal innovation, Roman, is the FDA.
sentences.zh: 但罗曼，推动这种对命名创新不懈追求的主要因素是FDA。

sentences.en: And so, why does the FDA do this?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么FDA要这么做呢？

sentences.en: Like, what are the rules?
sentences.zh: 规则是什么？

sentences.en: So, two big things to focus on here.
sentences.zh: 这里有两个重点需要关注。

sentences.en: Number one, what a drug seems to be promising.
sentences.zh: 第一，药物看起来承诺了什么。

sentences.en: The FDA doesn't want a name to sound like, oh, this is some miracle drug.
sentences.zh: FDA不希望名字听起来像是什么灵丹妙药。

sentences.en: So, no big claims in the name.
sentences.zh: 所以，名字里不能有夸大的宣传。

sentences.en: I'm sure you're familiar with Flomax.
sentences.zh: 我相信你对Flomax很熟悉。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I don't remember what it does.
sentences.zh: 我不记得它是治什么的了。

sentences.en: Flomax is for BPH.
sentences.zh: Flomax是治BPH的。

sentences.en: That is, benign prostatic hyperplasia.
sentences.zh: 也就是良性前列腺增生。

sentences.en: That same enlarged prostate condition that was the very first inspiration for the name Viagra.
sentences.zh: 正是那种前列腺肥大的症状，最初激发了Viagra这个名字的灵感。

sentences.en: So, maximum flow.
sentences.zh: 所以，最大流量（Maximum flow）。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Flomax.
sentences.zh: Flomax。

sentences.en: Simple, right?
sentences.zh: 很简单，对吧？

sentences.en: Simple.
sentences.zh: 很简单。

sentences.en: So, that name was approved in the late 90s, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我想那个名字是在90年代末获批的。

sentences.en: And that name is an example of one that probably today would be more challenged.
sentences.zh: 那个名字在今天可能就会受到更多质疑。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Um, because, and this is me speculating, I have no data to say this, but based on the guidance,
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为——这是我的推测，我没有数据支持——但根据指导方针，

sentences.en: you know, what is maximum flow, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，什么是最大流量，对吧？

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: I know how to determine maximum flow.
sentences.zh: 我知道怎么测定最大流量。

sentences.en: Go ahead.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: Pissing conteSt.
sentences.zh: 比尿远大赛。

sentences.en: Oh, geez.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Anyway, that's why Scott, when he talks about these drugs, is he's pretty circumspect.
sentences.zh: 总之，这就是为什么斯科特在谈论这些药物时非常谨慎的原因。

sentences.en: Like, he'll be like, he'll name a drug and then be like, it comes from this.
sentences.zh: 比如，他会给药起个名字，然后说，这是从这儿来的。

sentences.en: I mean, if you were potentially able to extrapolate that connotation, um, because nobody wants
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你能推断出那种内涵，嗯，因为没人想

sentences.en: to come right out and say, like, you know, take, you'll definitely sleep through the night
sentences.zh: 直接说出来，比如，你知道，吃了这个，你肯定能一觉睡到天亮

sentences.en: at all.
sentences.zh: 之类的。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: It's on sale.
sentences.zh: 它在售。

sentences.en: Um, you know, they want some plausible deniability.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，他们想要某种合理的推诿空间。
